latest_nl_proof: Interpret the sign convention in T_t as follows: +1 means apply U and -1 means apply D. For a vector v=(v_1,...,v_L), write rev(v)=(v_L,...,v_1), and write c dot y for the usual dot product. For the induction only, let Alt_0^+=Alt_0^- be the empty sign string. I prove the following stronger statement by induction on k>=0: for every length L>=1 there exists a positive nondecreasing vector c_{L,k} of length L such that for every nonnegative vector y of length L, (i) if y is nondecreasing, then Total(T_t(y)) <= c_{L,k} dot y for every sign string t of length k, while Total(T_{Alt_k^-}(y)) = c_{L,k} dot y; if y is nonconstant, equality holds only for t=Alt_k^-; (ii) if y is nonincreasing, then Total(T_t(y)) <= rev(c_{L,k}) dot y for every sign string t of length k, while Total(T_{Alt_k^+}(y)) = rev(c_{L,k}) dot y; if y is nonconstant, equality holds only for t=Alt_k^+. The lemma is the case L=m and k=r. Base case k=0: the only sign string is the empty string, and c_{L,0}=(1,...,1) works because Total(T_empty(y))=Total(y)=c_{L,0} dot y. Now assume the statement holds for k and all lengths. Fix L, and let c=c_{L+1,k}. Define b=c_{L,k+1} by b_i = sum_{j=L+2-i}^{L+1} c_j for 1<=i<=L. Since c is positive, b_{i+1}-b_i = c_{L+1-i} > 0, so b is positive and strictly increasing, hence nondecreasing. Also, for every y=(y_1,...,y_L), expanding the definitions gives c dot U(y) = sum_{j=1}^{L+1} c_j sum_{i=1}^{j-1} y_i = sum_{i=1}^L (sum_{j=i+1}^{L+1} c_j) y_i = rev(b) dot y, and rev(c) dot D(y) = sum_{j=1}^{L+1} c_{L+2-j} sum_{i=j}^L y_i = sum_{i=1}^L (sum_{j=1}^i c_{L+2-j}) y_i = b dot y. Now let y be nonnegative and nondecreasing, and let t=(eps,u) with eps in {+1,-1} and u of length k. Since U(y)_{j+1}-U(y)_j = y_j >= 0, U(y) is nonnegative and nondecreasing; hence if eps=+1, the induction hypothesis gives Total(T_t(y)) = Total(T_u(U(y))) <= c dot U(y) = rev(b) dot y. Since D(y)_j-D(y)_{j+1} = y_j >= 0, D(y) is nonnegative and nonincreasing; hence if eps=-1, the induction hypothesis gives Total(T_t(y)) = Total(T_u(D(y))) <= rev(c) dot D(y) = b dot y. Because b is strictly increasing and y is nondecreasing, b dot y - rev(b) dot y = sum_{i=1}^{floor(L/2)} (b_{L+1-i}-b_i)(y_{L+1-i}-y_i) >= 0. If y is nonconstant, then y_L>y_1, so the i=1 term is positive; hence b dot y > rev(b) dot y. Therefore Total(T_t(y)) <= b dot y for every t. Also Alt_{k+1}^- = (-1,Alt_k^+), so Total(T_{Alt_{k+1}^-}(y)) = Total(T_{Alt_k^+}(D(y))) = rev(c) dot D(y) = b dot y, by the induction hypothesis. Thus b dot y is the maximum. If y is nonconstant and equality holds for some t, then the strict inequality b dot y > rev(b) dot y forces eps=-1. Since y is nonnegative and nonconstant, Total(y)>0, so D(y)_1=Total(y)>0=D(y)_{L+1}; hence D(y) is nonconstant. The induction hypothesis applied to D(y) then forces u=Alt_k^+, so t=Alt_{k+1}^-. This proves part (i) for k+1. For part (ii), let y be nonnegative and nonincreasing. If eps=+1, then U(y) is nonnegative and nondecreasing, so Total(T_t(y)) <= c dot U(y) = rev(b) dot y. If eps=-1, then D(y) is nonnegative and nonincreasing, so Total(T_t(y)) <= rev(c) dot D(y) = b dot y. Since y is nonincreasing, rev(b) dot y - b dot y = sum_{i=1}^{floor(L/2)} (b_{L+1-i}-b_i)(y_i-y_{L+1-i}) >= 0, and if y is nonconstant then y_1>y_L, so again the i=1 term is positive; hence rev(b) dot y > b dot y. Therefore Total(T_t(y)) <= rev(b) dot y for every t. Also Alt_{k+1}^+ = (+1,Alt_k^-), so Total(T_{Alt_{k+1}^+}(y)) = Total(T_{Alt_k^-}(U(y))) = c dot U(y) = rev(b) dot y. If y is nonconstant and equality holds, then eps=+1. Also U(y)_1=0 < Total(y)=U(y)_{L+1}, so U(y) is nonconstant; hence the induction hypothesis forces u=Alt_k^-, so t=Alt_{k+1}^+. This proves part (ii). The induction is complete. Taking L=m and k=r gives exactly the statement: if x is nonincreasing, then Total(T_t(x)) <= Total(T_{Alt_r^+}(x)) for every sign string t of length r, with equality iff t=Alt_r^+ when x is nonconstant; and if x is nondecreasing, then Total(T_t(x)) <= Total(T_{Alt_r^-}(x)) for every t, with equality iff t=Alt_r^- when x is nonconstant.
role_in_parent: This is the main optimization lemma. It is applied to the state after the first sign to force the rest of the sign pattern to alternate, and its equality clause yields uniqueness.
statement_nl: Fix positive integers m and r. Define U, D, T_t, Total, Alt_r^+, and Alt_r^- exactly as follows: if y=(y_1,...,y_ell), then U(y) and D(y) are length ell+1 vectors given by U(y)_j = sum_{i=1}^{j-1} y_i and D(y)_j = sum_{i=j}^{ell} y_i for 1 <= j <= ell+1, with empty sums equal to 0; for a sign string t=(t_1,...,t_r) with each t_q in {+1,-1}, T_t(x) is obtained by applying U or D successively according to the signs; Alt_r^+=(+1,-1,+1,-1,...) and Alt_r^-=(-1,+1,-1,+1,...) have length r; and Total(y) is the sum of the entries of y. Let x be a nonnegative vector of length m. If x is nonincreasing, then for every sign string t of length r, Total(T_t(x)) <= Total(T_{Alt_r^+}(x)). If x is nonconstant, equality holds if and only if t = Alt_r^+. If x is nondecreasing, then for every sign string t of length r, Total(T_t(x)) <= Total(T_{Alt_r^-}(x)). If x is nonconstant, equality holds if and only if t = Alt_r^-.

domain_restrictions: m and r are positive integers.
The vector x has length m and all entries are nonnegative.
Nonincreasing means x_1 is at least x_2, x_2 is at least x_3, and so on through x_m.
Nondecreasing means x_1 is at most x_2, x_2 is at most x_3, and so on through x_m.
Nonconstant means not all entries of x are equal.
A sign string t has length r and each entry is either plus one or minus one.
For y of length ell, U(y) and D(y) each have length ell plus 1.
The text does not explicitly state which sign corresponds to U and which corresponds to D, although an intended convention is required for T_t.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For a nonnegative length-m vector x, the maximum possible total after applying r successive choices between the two sum-expansion operators is achieved by the alternating sign pattern. When x is nonincreasing, the maximizing pattern is the alternating string starting with plus one; when x is nondecreasing, the maximizing pattern is the alternating string starting with minus one. If x is not constant, this maximizer is unique in each case.
quantifier_order: Fix positive integers m and r.
For every vector y of length ell, U(y) and D(y) are defined by the stated prefix-sum and suffix-sum formulas, with empty sums equal to 0.
For every sign string t of length r, T_t is formed by successive application of U or D according to the signs in t.

For every nonnegative vector x of length m, if x is nonincreasing then for every sign string t of length r, Total(T_t(x)) is at most Total(T_Alt_r_plus(x)); if x is nonconstant, equality holds exactly when t is Alt_r_plus.

For every nonnegative vector x of length m, if x is nondecreasing then for every sign string t of length r, Total(T_t(x)) is at most Total(T_Alt_r_minus(x)); if x is nonconstant, equality holds exactly when t is Alt_r_minus.

witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses in the statement.
In the equality clauses, the only specified sign string is the alternating one determined solely by r, so the equality case is a uniqueness claim about t rather than a witness-existence claim.
